features.method: Walked along the Jinping traffic tunnel (OSM ways 681216327 and 653641019, the twin bores) from both portals, using the distances CJPL's own review paper states: 8.8 km from the west portal and 8.7 km from the east portal to CJPL-I's main hall. This gives four independent point estimates (2 bores x 2 directions of measurement); they agree to within 6-81 m of their centroid (mean pairwise spread ~39 m), which is used here as the coordinate. This is anchored entirely on the OSM tunnel line (accuracy_m 25) and the paper's own portal distances, not on any pre-existing site-level campus point, so it does not rest on a coarser anchor than its own accuracy_m. The tunnel-derived point sits 124 m from the campus-grade geocoder point already on record for this site (well inside that point's own precision_m) — consistent, not a contradiction — see worklog for the site-coordinate-correction recommendation.
features.name: CJPL-I main hall (derived point, walked along the traffic tunnel)

provenance.locator: Section II: "The distances to the east and west ends of the tunnel entrance are 8.7 km and 8.8 km, respectively."
provenance.note: Point stands in for the ~6.5 m x 6.5 m x 40 m main hall; not a trace of the hall's own footprint (no plan with that footprint's orientation along the tunnel axis was fetched this session).
provenance.quote: Construction of Phase I of CJPL (CJPL-I) started in December 2009 near the center of one of the Jinping traffic tunnels, where the vertical rock overburden is maximal ... The distances to the east and west ends of the tunnel entrance are 8.7 km and 8.8 km, respectively.

features.method: Walked along the Jinping traffic tunnel (OSM ways 681216327 and 653641019, the twin bores) from both portals, using the distances CJPL's own review paper states for CJPL-II: 8.3 km from the west portal and 9.2 km from the east portal (Table III). This gives four independent point estimates (2 bores x 2 directions of measurement); they agree to within 5-41 m of their centroid (mean pairwise spread ~39 m), which is used here as the coordinate. This is anchored entirely on the OSM tunnel line (accuracy_m 25) and the paper's own portal distances, not on any pre-existing site-level campus point, so it does not rest on a coarser anchor than its own accuracy_m. The tunnel-derived point sits 622 m from the campus-grade geocoder point already on record for this site (well inside that point's own precision_m of 2500 m) — consistent, not a contradiction — see worklog for the site-coordinate-correction recommendation. Internally consistent with the CJPL-I point: the two tunnel-derived positions are exactly 500.0 m apart, matching the sourced 'CJPL-II is 500 m west of CJPL-I' statement by construction (the two portal-distance pairs, 8.8/8.7 km and 8.3/9.2 km, differ by exactly 0.5 km) — not treated as an independent checks[] row for that reason, per the same reasoning already established for this style of walked derivation.
features.name: CJPL-II experimental halls (derived point, walked along the traffic tunnel)

provenance.locator: Table III: "Main Road Tunnels ... 9.2(8.3) km from East(West) Entrance"; Section VI: "CJPL-II is located 500 m to the west of CJPL-I"
provenance.note: Point stands in for the four-cavern hall complex's centre; not a trace of the individual caverns' footprints (their exact offsets from this reference point along the connecting tunnels were not fetched to a level that supports drawing polygons).
provenance.quote: CJPL-II is located 500 m to the west of CJPL-I, along the same road tunnel. It will have four caverns, each with dimensions of 14 m (width) x 14 m (height) x 130 m (length)

features.method: OpenStreetMap way 681216327 (highway=tertiary, tunnel=yes, name '锦屏二级水电站交通隙洞', 20 nodes), kept verbatim from the west portal (28.2151356 N, 101.6423797 E) to the east portal (28.1317909 N, 101.7889765 E). A near-identical parallel bore (way 653641019, same name, 19 nodes) lies ~65-70 m away throughout and is not separately drawn (CJPL's own papers describe the pair as 'two 17.5-km-long traffic tunnels'; only one is needed to show the route to scale). accuracy_m 25 m reflects a standard OSM tunnel-line trace of a twin road-tunnel pair; the deep-mountain middle section is represented by OSM as a single long straight chord (vertices 8-9 of the 20), consistent with a bored traffic tunnel's genuinely straight alignment rather than a data-quality gap.

summary.plain: China's deepest underground physics laboratory, built beside a hydropower traffic tunnel more than two kilometres under Jinping Mountain in Sichuan. CJPL-I and the newer, larger CJPL-II sit half a kilometre apart along the same tunnel.
